sections.name: Databases and Data Engineering
sections.outcome: Design, build, query, and operate data systems that turn heterogeneous inputs into reliable relational, nonrelational, and analytical data products.
includes: Selecting data representations and storage models from access and integrity requirements.
Integrating schema-governed data handling, database operations, pipelines, and distributed data design.
excludes: Statistical modeling or machine-learning training after data preparation.
Application features whose central challenge is not data storage, transformation, or retrieval.

sample_tasks.instruction: Turn a small list of customer facts into named fields and records suitable for storage.

Design a data platform that ingests changing JSON and CSV feeds, validates and loads an analytical relational model, maintains a graph view of entity relationships, supports specified queries, and can be monitored and safely recovered.

sections.name: Schema-Governed Structured Data
sections.outcome: Interpret schemas and transform documents or generated content into complete, correctly typed structured representations.
includes: Mapping explicit or permitted values into constrained records.
Serializing nested records and integrating facts from prose and tables.
excludes: Designing persistent database schemas or indexes.
Scheduling recurring ingestion and transformation jobs.

sample_tasks.instruction: Represent three stated attributes as a typed record with the requested field names.
Interpret a nested schema, integrate related facts from prose and several tables, resolve permitted omissions, and serialize the resulting records as JSON, XML, and a flattened CSV extract.

sections.name: Schema-Governed Record Construction
sections.outcome: Use structural and value constraints to extract or generate valid typed records.
includes: Required and optional fields, types, enums, bounds, patterns, nullability, arrays, and nested objects.
Distinguishing source-supported extraction from explicitly requested value generation.
excludes: Format-specific escaping and markup syntax.
Database normalization and physical storage design.

sample_tasks.instruction: Read a small object schema and list the required fields with their permitted types.

Given a nested schema and a partially specified business document, identify every applicable constraint, map supported facts, and construct permitted values for required fields that the task explicitly asks you to generate.

sections.name: Schema Constraint Interpretation
sections.outcome: Determine whether record shapes and values satisfy explicit structural and scalar constraints.
includes: Required properties, additional-property rules, nested cardinality, and nullable fields.
Type, enum, range, pattern, and date-time constraints.
excludes: Inferring facts from narrative documents.
Choosing tables, indexes, or storage engines.

sample_tasks.instruction: For a schema with one required integer field and one optional string field, identify which of three candidate records has the permitted shape.
Audit a nested record against required-field, additional-property, type, enum, numeric-bound, pattern, date, array, and nullability constraints, reporting each violated constraint.

sections.name: Grounded Record Mapping
sections.outcome: Map explicitly supported facts from prose or simple tables into the correct fields of a supplied schema without inventing unsupported facts.
includes: Entity, quantity, date, status, classification, and contact-field extraction.
Type conversion and omission or null handling when the schema permits it.
excludes: Creating plausible values when generation is requested.
Combining many heterogeneous tables into one coordinated dataset.

sample_tasks.instruction: Map an explicitly stated place name and population into two correctly typed fields of a supplied schema.

Extract a property description into a nested record containing location, numeric attributes, status, amenities, financing preference, and a constrained contact method while retaining only supported facts.

sections.name: Schema-Constrained Instance Generation
sections.outcome: Create plausible records that satisfy a supplied schema when values are not source-bound.
includes: Generating compatible scalar, array, object, and nullable values.
Maintaining cross-field plausibility while obeying strict constraints.
excludes: Claiming generated values were extracted from a source.
Designing or modifying the supplied schema.

sample_tasks.instruction: Generate one object containing a required name and a bounded integer according to a small schema.
Generate a plausible transportation record with nested endpoints, junction arrays, concurrency records, enums, nullable values, and no undeclared properties.

sections.name: Structured Format Serialization
sections.outcome: Serialize equivalent typed data accurately across hierarchical and tabular formats.
includes: Correct representation of nested objects, arrays, scalars, nulls, and special characters.
Reshaping data when the target format cannot directly preserve the source hierarchy.
excludes: Extracting unstated facts from source documents.
Database import, transaction, or query execution.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a two-field record as valid JSON.
Serialize one nested dataset as JSON, YAML, and XML, then produce a CSV projection with a documented flattening convention and correct escaping.

sections.name: JSON and YAML Serialization
sections.outcome: Represent nested typed records as syntactically correct JSON or YAML without changing their logical structure.
includes: Objects, sequences, scalar types, nulls, quoting, and indentation.
Preserving schema-required names and nesting.
excludes: XML element and attribute design.
Flattening nested structures into table cells.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a record containing a string, integer, boolean, and null as valid JSON.
Produce a YAML document for a deeply nested route record containing termini, junction arrays, concurrent segments, nullable fields, and constrained scalar values.

sections.name: XML Serialization
sections.outcome: Represent nested records and repeated entities as a single well-formed XML document with the required structure.
includes: Elements, attributes when requested, repeated records, escaping, and valid nesting.
Mapping typed object and array structures into XML.
excludes: DTD or XML Schema language design unless explicitly requested.
HTML presentation markup.

sample_tasks.instruction: Serialize a name and publication date beneath one XML root element.

Create a well-formed XML document for an institutional report containing authors, funding records, nested metrics, components, assessments, and repeated applications according to a supplied structure.

sections.name: CSV Flattening and Escaping
sections.outcome: Convert structured records into parseable CSV while applying an explicit, consistent policy for nested or repeated values.
includes: Header selection, row construction, delimiter quoting, embedded quotes, and line breaks.
Consistent serialization of arrays and nested values within cells.
excludes: Relational normalization into multiple persistent tables.
Spreadsheet formatting, formulas, or charts.

sample_tasks.instruction: Write a CSV header and one row whose text field contains a comma and quotation marks.
Flatten a YAML record containing arrays, booleans, punctuation-rich text, and nested footnotes into a complete CSV row with stable column names and parseable escaping.

sections.name: Complex Document Integration
sections.outcome: Integrate related facts from multiple prose sections and heterogeneous tables into a coherent nested collection of records.
includes: Reconciling entity identity across sections and tables.
Preserving relationships among summary objects and repeated detail records.
excludes: Joining already loaded database tables with SQL.
Adding facts that cannot be supported by the supplied material.

sample_tasks.instruction: Combine a prose summary and one two-row table into a parent record with a related child array.
Integrate a season overview, staff details, rankings, standings, recruiting rows, and a schedule into one coherent nested dataset with consistent team identities and correctly typed values.

sections.name: Relational Databases
sections.outcome: Design relational schemas, express precise SQL retrieval and modification logic, and diagnose operational or integrity failures.
includes: Logical and physical schema design, querying, transactions, connectivity, and execution diagnosis.
Reasoning about keys, constraints, indexes, generated statements, and concurrent changes.
excludes: Document-store or graph-native modeling.
End-to-end orchestration of multi-stage data pipelines.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define a table with a primary key and retrieve rows matching one condition.

Design and index a normalized order schema, write transactional load and analytical queries for it, configure an application connection, and diagnose a captured constraint failure under concurrent updates.

sections.name: SQL Querying
sections.outcome: Write SQL that retrieves, relates, summarizes, and ranks relational data with correct row and grouping semantics.
includes: Projection, filtering, ordering, joins, grouping, subqueries, common table expressions, and window functions.
Handling nulls and duplicate rows deliberately.
excludes: DDL schema design and index selection.
Transaction boundaries and write-conflict handling.

sample_tasks.instruction: Select two columns from a table, filter by a status value, and order by a timestamp.
Join customers, orders, and payments; aggregate monthly revenue; retain customers above a threshold; rank them within region; and return ties and missing payments according to stated rules.

sections.name: Single-Table SQL Queries
sections.outcome: Retrieve and reshape rows from one table using precise projection, filtering, expression, null, and ordering rules.
includes: SELECT expressions, aliases, predicates, sorting, limits, and null handling.
Distinctness and simple scalar calculations.
excludes: Joins and grouped multi-row summaries.
Inserts, updates, and deletes.

sample_tasks.instruction: Select the name column from active records in one table.
Return the latest twenty eligible products from one table with computed discounted prices, explicit null handling, deduplication, and deterministic ordering.

sections.name: Joins and Aggregation
sections.outcome: Combine related tables and compute grouped summaries without introducing unintended loss or duplication.
includes: Inner and outer joins, join cardinality, GROUP BY, aggregate functions, and HAVING.
Counting or summing under duplicate and null semantics.
excludes: Window functions and recursive queries.
Physical denormalization for performance.

sample_tasks.instruction: Join an order table to a customer table by customer identifier and return one field from each.

Compute per-department headcount and total payroll while retaining empty departments, avoiding duplicate employees introduced by a secondary assignment table, and filtering groups by a stated threshold.

sections.name: Compositional and Analytical SQL
sections.outcome: Express multi-stage and row-relative analysis with subqueries, common table expressions, set operations, and window functions.
includes: Ranking, running totals, lag or lead comparisons, partitioned calculations, and recursive traversal when relationally encoded.
Structuring complex logic into auditable query stages.
excludes: Dashboard presentation and statistical inference.
Graph-native traversal languages.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a common table expression that filters an existing grouped query before its final projection.
For each account and month, calculate revenue, running revenue, change from the prior month, and rank within its region while preserving months with no transactions.

sections.name: Relational Schema Design
sections.outcome: Translate data and access requirements into integrity-preserving logical tables and fit-for-purpose physical indexes.
includes: Entities, relationships, keys, constraints, normalization, data types, and index selection.
Evaluating integrity and query-plan consequences of design choices.
excludes: Nonrelational aggregate or graph models.
Pipeline scheduling and operational alerting.

sample_tasks.instruction: Separate repeated customer details from orders and link the resulting tables with a key.

Design a normalized subscription-billing schema with temporal prices and payment attempts, define its integrity constraints, and choose indexes for the stated lookup, renewal, and reporting workloads.

sections.name: Logical Schema and Integrity Constraints
sections.outcome: Model entities and relationships as normalized tables with suitable types, keys, and declarative constraints.
includes: Primary, foreign, unique, check, and nullability constraints.
Resolving repeating groups and update anomalies through normalization.
excludes: Index access paths and storage layout.
Application-only validation that cannot protect the database.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a primary key and add a foreign key between two simple tables.
Model products, suppliers, warehouses, inventory lots, and supplier-specific prices as normalized tables with cardinalities, keys, temporal rules, and constraints that prevent invalid states.

sections.name: Index and Access-Path Design
sections.outcome: Choose and assess relational indexes from concrete query, write, selectivity, and ordering requirements.
includes: Composite key order, covering indexes, uniqueness, filtered indexes, and write amplification.
Relating predicates, joins, sorting, and grouping to useful access paths.
excludes: Changing logical facts solely to imitate an index.
Vendor-specific tuning without a stated workload.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose an index for equality lookup on a foreign key in an existing schema.
Given a normalized schema, query patterns, column selectivities, and write rates, propose a minimal index set and explain which predicates, joins, and orderings each index serves.

sections.name: Reliable Relational Data Changes
sections.outcome: Apply multi-row database changes atomically while preserving integrity under failure and concurrency.
includes: Transactional inserts, updates, deletes, upserts, isolation, locking, and conflict handling.
Reasoning about rollback, retries, and invariant preservation.
excludes: Read-only analytical querying.
Workflow retries outside the database boundary.

sample_tasks.instruction: Place two dependent updates in one transaction so either both persist or neither does.
Implement concurrent inventory reservation and payment recording so overselling, partial commits, duplicate requests, deadlocks, and safe retries are handled without violating database invariants.

sections.name: Transactional Mutation
sections.outcome: Implement inserts, updates, deletes, and upserts with atomic boundaries and constraint-preserving failure behavior.
includes: Transaction start, commit, rollback, affected-row checks, and ordered dependent writes.
Idempotent keys and safe upsert semantics within a database.
excludes: Isolation anomalies caused by competing transactions.
Cross-system workflow compensation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Insert an invoice and its first line item in one transaction.
Apply a batch of account transfers using guarded updates, a durable request key, rollback on any invalid balance, and a result that distinguishes a replay from a new transfer.

sections.name: Concurrency and Isolation
sections.outcome: Choose and implement concurrency controls that prevent specified anomalies while allowing acceptable parallelism.
includes: Isolation levels, locks, optimistic versions, serialization failures, deadlocks, and retry boundaries.
Constructing interleavings that demonstrate or rule out anomalies.
excludes: General distributed consensus across independent databases.
Performance tuning unrelated to concurrent correctness.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a version predicate to an existing update so a stale writer is detected.

Analyze competing reservation and cancellation transactions, identify possible lost-update, write-skew, and deadlock interleavings, and choose isolation, locking, or optimistic retry rules that preserve the stated invariants.

sections.name: Database Connectivity and Diagnosis
sections.outcome: Establish database connections, observe executed statements, and trace integrity failures through application, schema, and runtime behavior.
includes: Driver and connection configuration, network and authentication checks, SQL logging, parameters, transactions, triggers, and constraint metadata.
Evidence-based isolation of the failing database operation.
excludes: Query optimization without an observed workload or symptom.
Generic application debugging unrelated to database interaction.

sample_tasks.instruction: Identify the server, database, authentication, and driver fields needed for a database connection.

Configure an application to reach a database on a custom endpoint, capture its generated parameterized statements, and diagnose an intermittent unique-constraint failure by reconciling logs, transaction state, triggers, indexes, and concurrent writes.

sections.name: Driver and Connection Configuration
sections.outcome: Construct and troubleshoot database connection settings for the chosen client, driver, endpoint, and authentication mode.
includes: Driver or provider syntax, host, port, instance, database, encryption, and credentials.
Separating client-format errors from DNS, routing, firewall, listener, and authentication failures.
excludes: SQL statement correctness after a connection succeeds.
Embedding secrets in examples or source code.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add an explicit nondefault port to a database connection configuration using the selected driver's syntax.

Configure a legacy application to connect through an installed driver to a remote database on a nonstandard port, then provide ordered checks that distinguish provider, network, listener, encryption, and authentication failures.

sections.name: Executed-Statement Observability
sections.outcome: Capture the SQL text, bound parameters, timing, transaction context, and outcome of database commands issued by an application or data-access layer.
includes: Client logging, server tracing, query-history facilities, and correlation identifiers.
Distinguishing generated commands from pending in-memory changes.
excludes: Guessing statements from object state when capture is available.
Full application observability outside database calls.

sample_tasks.instruction: Enable command logging for one database context and capture a single parameterized statement.
Design a diagnostic capture that correlates application operations with executed SQL, parameters, transaction boundaries, durations, and server errors while protecting sensitive parameter values.

sections.name: Integrity Failure Diagnosis
sections.outcome: Explain and isolate database constraint failures by tracing the executed change through schema objects and concurrent or implicit behavior.
includes: Unique, foreign-key, check, and null violations caused by direct statements, triggers, computed values, stale mappings, or races.
Comparing runtime metadata with the schema assumed by the application.
excludes: Suppressing exceptions without identifying the violated invariant.
Connection failures that occur before statement execution.

sample_tasks.instruction: Match a captured insert error to the named unique constraint and identify the conflicting key values.

Diagnose why an update to a nonindexed timestamp intermittently reports a duplicate-key violation by examining the generated statement, parameters, actual index definition, triggers, computed columns, identity mapping, transaction behavior, and concurrent changes.

sections.name: ETL and Data Pipelines
sections.outcome: Build repeatable pipelines that ingest changing sources, transform and validate records, orchestrate dependencies, and deliver trustworthy analytical data.
includes: Batch and incremental ingestion, cleaning, quality controls, orchestration, recovery, and warehouse loading.
Operational guarantees across repeated and partial executions.
excludes: One-off manual format conversion with no persistent flow.
Model training or downstream business analysis.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define an extract, transform, and load sequence for one small source file and destination table.

Build a monitored pipeline that combines daily files with an incremental change feed, standardizes and validates records, updates dimensional and fact tables idempotently, and recovers correctly from a mid-run failure.

sections.name: Data Ingestion
sections.outcome: Acquire source data in batch or incrementally while preserving identity, ordering, checkpoints, and replayability.
includes: Files, APIs, database extracts, change streams, source metadata, and ingestion boundaries.
Detecting duplicates, late arrivals, schema changes, and incomplete input.
excludes: Business-rule transformation after acquisition.
Dashboard refresh and analytical presentation.

sample_tasks.instruction: Read one delimited file and attach its source name and ingestion time to each record.
Ingest an initial collection of partitioned files and then apply ordered changes from a source database using checkpoints, duplicate detection, late-arrival handling, and a safe replay procedure.

sections.name: Batch Ingestion
sections.outcome: Load bounded files or snapshots completely and repeatably while retaining provenance and detecting malformed or duplicate inputs.
includes: File discovery, partition selection, parsing, manifests, source metadata, and batch completeness checks.
Atomic publication or quarantine of a bounded load.
excludes: Continuous change streams and offsets.
Downstream business transformations.

sample_tasks.instruction: Load one CSV file into typed records and retain its filename on each record.
Ingest a date-partitioned delivery of compressed files using a manifest, reject malformed rows, detect duplicate files and records, verify completeness, and publish the batch atomically.

sections.name: Incremental and Change-Data Ingestion
sections.outcome: Capture new, changed, and deleted records incrementally with correct ordering, checkpoints, and replay semantics.
includes: High-water marks, log positions, change-data capture, tombstones, late changes, and snapshot handoff.
Restarting without gaps or unintended duplication.
excludes: Full snapshot loading when no incremental state exists.
Applying business aggregations to captured changes.

sample_tasks.instruction: Extend a snapshot load to fetch records newer than a stored high-water mark.
Design a snapshot-to-change-stream handoff that applies inserts, updates, and deletes in order, persists checkpoints atomically, handles late events, and can replay after a consumer failure.

sections.name: Transformation and Data Quality
sections.outcome: Standardize heterogeneous records and enforce measurable quality rules without hiding rejected or altered data.
includes: Type normalization, missing-value policy, deduplication, entity matching, validation, quarantine, and reconciliation.
Recording transformation and quality evidence.
excludes: Source transport and checkpoint management.
Schema design driven only by query performance.

sample_tasks.instruction: Normalize two date formats into one typed date field and flag unparseable values.

Standardize customer feeds with inconsistent names, addresses, identifiers, dates, and units; resolve duplicates; enforce field and cross-record rules; quarantine failures; and reconcile accepted totals to the inputs.

sections.name: Data Cleaning and Standardization
sections.outcome: Convert inconsistent source values into canonical typed records using explicit, auditable transformation rules.
includes: Parsing, casing, whitespace, dates, units, categories, missing values, deduplication, and record linkage.
Retaining original values or transformation provenance when needed.
excludes: Silently inventing missing business facts.
Assessing aggregate completeness or source-to-target totals.

sample_tasks.instruction: Trim whitespace and normalize two textual date formats into one date type.
Clean overlapping contact feeds by standardizing names, phones, addresses, categories, dates, and units, then resolve likely duplicates using explicit matching and survivorship rules.

sections.name: Data Quality Controls
sections.outcome: Define and apply field, record, relational, and aggregate checks that make bad or incomplete data observable and actionable.
includes: Validity, completeness, uniqueness, referential integrity, anomaly thresholds, quarantine, and reconciliation.
Quality metrics and acceptance gates.
excludes: Cosmetic formatting with no correctness implication.
Repairing values without an explicit transformation rule.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a required-field and allowed-range check to cleaned records, routing failures to quarantine.

Create a quality gate for an order load that checks schema validity, key uniqueness, customer references, temporal consistency, amount reconciliation, anomaly thresholds, and accepted-versus-rejected counts.

sections.name: Pipeline Orchestration and Recovery
sections.outcome: Coordinate dependent pipeline stages so scheduled and retried executions are ordered, idempotent, observable, and recoverable.
includes: Dependency graphs, partitions, scheduling, backfills, retries, checkpoints, alerts, and recovery.
Distinguishing task success from complete data-product readiness.
excludes: Transformation logic specific to individual fields.
Database transaction isolation inside a single task.

sample_tasks.instruction: Run a load task only after its extraction task succeeds.

Orchestrate a partitioned daily pipeline with dependency-aware scheduling, idempotent writes, bounded retries, backfills, readiness checks, metrics, alerts, and restart behavior after partial publication.

sections.name: Dependency and Partition Scheduling
sections.outcome: Express and execute pipeline dependencies, schedules, partitions, and backfills without processing data before its prerequisites are ready.
includes: Directed acyclic task graphs, partition keys, calendars, readiness conditions, and bounded parallelism.
Planning backfills across dependent partitions.
excludes: Retry safety and duplicate-write prevention.
Field-level transformation rules.

sample_tasks.instruction: Define a three-stage dependency order for extract, transform, and load tasks.
Schedule hourly events and daily reference data into regional daily outputs, including readiness conditions, partition mappings, concurrency limits, and a backfill plan for a missed week.

sections.name: Idempotent Pipeline Execution
sections.outcome: Make repeated or resumed pipeline executions converge on the same target state without duplicate effects.
includes: Stable run and record keys, atomic replacement, merge semantics, checkpoints, and safe retry boundaries.
Handling partial output from prior attempts.
excludes: Business deduplication of genuinely distinct source records.
Concurrency control confined to one transactional application request.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a stable file identifier so rerunning an existing file load does not append duplicate rows.
Design a partition load that stages output, merges by stable keys, publishes atomically, records checkpoints, and safely resumes after failures before and after publication.

sections.name: Pipeline Monitoring and Recovery
sections.outcome: Detect pipeline failures or degraded data delivery and recover the affected scope without corrupting completed work.
includes: Freshness, volume, latency, error, and quality signals; structured logs; lineage-aware impact; alerts; and runbooks.
Retry, replay, rollback, and selective recomputation decisions.
excludes: Infrastructure monitoring unrelated to data delivery.
Blindly restarting jobs without determining the safe recovery boundary.

sample_tasks.instruction: Add a freshness metric and alert to an idempotent daily load.
Diagnose a pipeline whose row count dropped after one upstream partition failed, identify affected downstream products through lineage, and specify safe retry, replay, rollback, and validation steps.

sections.name: Analytical Modeling and Loading
sections.outcome: Shape transformed data into analytical models and load them while preserving grain, history, and reproducibility.
includes: Facts, dimensions, measures, surrogate keys, historical attributes, incremental merges, and late-arriving data.
Declaring table grain and source-to-target mappings.
excludes: Operational schemas optimized for transactional writes.
Visualization and business interpretation of the resulting metrics.

sample_tasks.instruction: Separate one event measure from its descriptive entity attributes into a fact and a dimension.
Design and incrementally load a sales model with conformed dimensions, declared fact grain, historical customer attributes, late-arriving events, surrogate keys, and reconciled measures.

sections.name: Dimensional Modeling
sections.outcome: Design fact and dimension tables whose grain, keys, measures, and historical behavior support specified analytical questions.
includes: Transaction, periodic snapshot, and accumulating snapshot facts; conformed dimensions; and slowly changing attributes.
Explicit grain and additive behavior.
excludes: Physical dashboard layouts.
Operational normalization without an analytical workload.

sample_tasks.instruction: Declare the grain of a purchase-line fact and identify its customer and product dimensions.
Model orders, shipments, returns, and inventory snapshots with conformed dimensions, appropriate fact types, additive measures, role-playing dates, and historical customer segments.

sections.name: Incremental Warehouse Loading
sections.outcome: Load analytical facts and dimensions incrementally while preserving key resolution, history, and source-to-target reconciliation.
includes: Surrogate-key lookup, slowly changing dimension updates, late facts, corrections, merges, and audit totals.
Ordering dimension and fact loads.
excludes: Designing source capture protocols.
Defining business metrics beyond what the target model requires.

sample_tasks.instruction: Resolve one incoming business key to an existing dimension surrogate key before inserting a fact.

Implement an incremental warehouse load that applies historical dimension changes, assigns surrogate keys, handles early and late facts, corrects prior records, and reconciles source counts and measures.

sections.name: NoSQL and Graph Data Systems
sections.outcome: Choose and design document, key-value, wide-column, or graph data systems from access patterns, relationship structure, scale, and consistency requirements.
includes: Aggregate and graph modeling, native queries, partitioning, replication, and transaction tradeoffs.
Making denormalization and duplication policies explicit.
excludes: Using a nonrelational store solely as an interchangeable relational database.
Search-engine indexing and vector retrieval unless part of the stated data model.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose between an embedded document and a separate related record for one read pattern.

Design a globally distributed service that uses document aggregates for profiles, key-addressed records for activity, and a graph for relationships, including queries, partition keys, replication, consistency, and update invariants.

sections.name: Document, Key-Value, and Wide-Column Modeling
sections.outcome: Model denormalized aggregates and key-addressed records around concrete read, write, and scale patterns.
includes: Embedding versus referencing, key composition, access-path tables, sparse columns, and controlled duplication.
Update and fan-out consequences of each model.
excludes: Arbitrary relational normalization transplanted unchanged.
Graph traversal as the primary access pattern.

sample_tasks.instruction: Model a user preference record as one key and one structured value.

Design a messaging model that stores conversation metadata as documents and messages in key-addressed or wide-column partitions, supporting inbox, conversation, pagination, retention, and unread-count access patterns.

sections.name: Document Data Modeling
sections.outcome: Define document aggregates, embedding boundaries, references, and update rules that serve specified access patterns.
includes: Nested objects and arrays, document identity, schema variation, embedding, referencing, and document-level atomicity.
Bounding document growth and duplication.
excludes: Key-only values with no internal queryable structure.
Multi-hop graph traversal.

sample_tasks.instruction: Embed a small shipping address inside an order document that is always read with the order.

Model a publishing system's articles, authors, revisions, comments, and tags as documents, choosing embedding or references for each relationship and accounting for growth, atomic updates, and required queries.

sections.name: Key-Value and Wide-Column Modeling
sections.outcome: Design keys, partitions, clustering order, and duplicated access paths for predictable key-based or range-based operations.
includes: Composite keys, hot-key avoidance, time buckets, clustering order, sparse attributes, and materialized query tables.
Write fan-out and retention by partition.
excludes: Ad hoc joins across arbitrary entities.
Graph-native relationship expansion.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a composite key that retrieves one customer's settings directly.

Design wide-column tables for device readings by device and time and alerts by region and severity, including partition bounds, clustering order, retention, hot-partition avoidance, and write fan-out.

sections.name: Graph Data Modeling and Querying
sections.outcome: Represent relationship-rich domains as graphs and express bounded traversals, paths, and neighborhood analyses over them.
includes: Node and edge identities, labels, direction, properties, constraints, indexes, and traversal semantics.
Controlling cycles, path length, duplication, and result cardinality.
excludes: Using graph storage for records with no relationship-driven queries.
Distributed partition and consistency policy.

sample_tasks.instruction: Represent two people and their directed employment relationships to one organization as nodes and edges.

Model accounts, devices, transactions, merchants, and shared identifiers as a graph, then query bounded suspicious paths and neighborhoods while preventing cyclic duplication and explaining the required constraints and indexes.

sections.name: Graph Schema Modeling
sections.outcome: Choose nodes, edges, direction, properties, labels, and identity constraints that preserve the semantics required by relationship-driven workloads.
includes: Promoting relationships or attributes to first-class graph entities when their identity or history matters.
Cardinality, temporal edges, uniqueness, and indexing entry points.
excludes: Writing traversal logic beyond simple model checks.
Document embedding decisions without graph queries.

sample_tasks.instruction: Model customers and products with a directed purchased edge carrying a timestamp.

Design a temporal supply-chain graph with organizations, facilities, products, shipments, ownership, and certifications, including identity rules, edge direction, properties, constraints, and indexed starting points.

sections.name: Graph Traversal Queries
sections.outcome: Write graph queries that return the intended paths, neighborhoods, or aggregates with explicit direction, bounds, and duplicate semantics.
includes: Pattern matching, variable-length traversal, shortest paths, cycle control, path predicates, aggregation, and result projection.
Selecting indexed starting nodes.
excludes: Redesigning the graph schema unless a query cannot be expressed correctly.
Unbounded exploration with unspecified termination.

sample_tasks.instruction: Query all products reached by one outgoing purchased edge from a specified customer.

Find bounded paths linking two accounts through shared devices or payment instruments, exclude repeated nodes, retain path evidence, aggregate risk by endpoint, and return deterministic ranked results.

sections.name: Distributed Data Placement and Consistency
sections.outcome: Choose partitioning, replication, and consistency mechanisms that meet stated scale, locality, availability, and invariant requirements.
includes: Shard keys, rebalancing, replica placement, quorum behavior, consistency levels, distributed transactions, and conflict resolution.
Evaluating behavior during lag, partitions, failover, and retries.
excludes: Single-node schema design with no distribution concerns.
Infrastructure provisioning unrelated to data semantics.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a partition key that keeps each tenant's bounded records together.

Design placement and consistency for a multi-region commerce dataset, including shard keys, replica locations, rebalancing, quorum or leader behavior, failover reads and writes, and transaction boundaries for inventory and orders.

sections.name: Partitioning and Replication
sections.outcome: Distribute records and replicas to balance load, bound partitions, preserve locality, and survive specified failures.
includes: Hash and range partitioning, composite shard keys, hotspots, resharding, replica placement, and failover topology.
Estimating fan-out for required queries.
excludes: Application-visible consistency guarantees except where needed to assess placement.
Logical entity modeling unrelated to distribution.

sample_tasks.instruction: Select a shard key for evenly distributing tenant records while retaining tenant-local reads.
Partition a high-volume event store by tenant and time, account for skew and range scans, specify resharding and replica placement, and analyze query fan-out and regional failure behavior.

sections.name: Distributed Consistency and Transactions
sections.outcome: Select consistency, quorum, conflict, and transaction semantics that preserve named invariants under concurrency and network failure.
includes: Strong, causal, session, and eventual guarantees; leader and quorum systems; conflict resolution; and atomic multi-record operations.
Explaining stale reads, retries, and ambiguous outcomes.
excludes: Partition-key selection except as a fixed input to consistency decisions.
Claiming consistency guarantees stronger than the system can provide.

sample_tasks.instruction: Choose a read guarantee that lets a user immediately observe their own successful profile update in an already partitioned store.

Specify consistency and transaction behavior for replicated balances, inventory, and user preferences during concurrent writes, replica lag, regional partitions, retries, and failover, preserving the stated invariants while identifying acceptable stale reads.
